text: The Patriots' offense imploded in Jacksonville on Sunday, with Drake Maye coughing up the ball three times—two interceptions and a lost fumble—in a brutish 35-6 defeat that has raised serious questions about both the young quarterback's early-season performance and whether the offensive scheme is actually working in his favor. Maye himself didn't shy away from accountability, calling his own play and the offense's overall effort "unacceptable" as he searches for answers during what's become a troubling stretch; meanwhile, beat writers' film breakdowns are digging into exactly what went wrong in the coverage splits and Maye's decision-making, with some analysis suggesting the Patriots may simply be using their quarterback in a way that's not maximizing his strengths. The Jaguars, led by rookie head coach Liam Coen and his team's three touchdown passes, demonstrated exactly the kind of response their coach had been preaching all week, while on the bright side for New England, Marcus Jones did record his first interception of the season in what was otherwise a forgettable performance for the entire organization.
